statuses.allowed: May be used and shipped; keep the licence and notice files that come with it.
statuses.review: HQ decides after the submission (exit code 2 if nothing is denied); there are no advance rulings (D63).
statuses.denied: Must not be used or shipped (exit code 1); there are no exceptions (D63). Packages of the organizer's common CUDA base (D52) are denied in a team bundle.

team_license.bundle: submission.json "license" is MIT, and participant_module/LICENSE holds the MIT licence text.
team_license.web: A LICENSE file at the root of the web code holds the MIT licence text, and every "license" in the team's own package.json files (root, sub-projects, workspaces), where present, is MIT.
team_license.rule: Decision D72 (2026-10-13), superseding D53 rule 1 of 2026-10-10, which also allowed Apache-2.0: the team's own work (Stage 1 code, rules and trained weights, adapters and fine-tunes included; Stage 2 web code) is licensed under MIT only, so that APCTT can use, combine and redistribute it later without a licence problem; Apache-2.0 is no longer accepted for the team's own work, and the participation terms' non-assertion covenant (D54) covers MIT's lack of an express patent licence. Anything else is denied, as is a missing or unreadable submission.json, a missing declaration and a missing or empty licence file. Only the plain identifier MIT counts; another identifier joined by OR or AND, an exception or added terms (MIT WITH Commons-Clause) make another licence and are denied. The same applies to a licence declared for team-trained weights. Third-party components and catalogue models keep their own licences (Apache-2.0 and MIT dependencies and models stay allowed, D53 and D64), and weights derived from a catalogue model stay subject to that model's licence as well: keep its LICENSE and NOTICE files with them. The checker reads the declared identifier and checks that the team's licence file holds the MIT text: its permission, condition and warranty paragraphs, compared after case, quotes, punctuation and white space are normalised; the Apache-2.0 text there is denied with a message that says so, and the MIT text together with the Apache-2.0 text is review.

allow_with_conditions.MPL-2.0: File-level copyleft: ship the MPL-covered files with the MPL-2.0 text and say where their source is; changes to those files stay under MPL-2.0.
allow_with_conditions.OFL-1.1: Fonts only: ship the OFL text with the font files; a modified or subset font must not use a Reserved Font Name.
allow_with_conditions.CC-BY-4.0: Icons, images, documents and data only: keep the attribution the licence requires.
allow_with_conditions.CC-BY-3.0: Icons, images, documents and data only: keep the attribution the licence requires.

GCC-exception-3.1.note: GCC Runtime Library Exception: covers GCC runtime libraries (libgcc, libstdc++, libgomp) inside compiled packages; keep their licence and notice files.

Font-exception-2.0.note: Font exception (for example the Liberation fonts in pdfjs-dist standard_fonts/, GPL-2.0 with Red Hat's font exception): ship the fonts unmodified with their licence file; do not modify or subset them.

rules.order: Each component's licence comes only from its declared metadata. Python: License-Expression, else the License :: classifiers (classifiers table), else the License field (license_strings table, then an SPDX expression). npm, models and data: the declared string (license_strings table, then an SPDX expression). Any other text is review: unrecognised licence string. Licence files are never parsed; only the team's own LICENSE (and a model copy's licence file) is checked for presence.
rules.spdx: Operators AND, OR and WITH in upper case, as SPDX requires; lower-case 'or' is text ('GPL v2 or later' is matched by the table, never read as OR). '+' and '-or-later' keep the family of the licence (GPL-2.0+ is GPL). A deprecated identifier in deprecated is read as its modern form wherever it appears (GPL-2.0-with-classpath-exception is GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0, GPL-2.0-with-GCC-exception is GPL-2.0-only WITH GCC-exception-2.0, which is not listed, so denied).
rules.restrictions: An identifier in restrictions (Commons Clause) adds a use restriction, it is not a licence: an expression that names one as a plain identifier anywhere is denied, also as an OR alternative (MIT OR Commons-Clause, Apache-2.0 AND Commons-Clause). As an exception (WITH Commons-Clause) it is denied by exceptions.
rules.OR: The most permissive allowed alternative counts (the licensee may choose). A paid or proprietary alternative (paid_alternatives, or a LicenseRef matching paid_alternative_patterns such as LicenseRef-Artifex-Commercial) is not a licence offered to everyone and never counts as a choice, so AGPL-3.0-only OR LicenseRef-Commercial is denied.
rules.WITH: Only the exceptions listed in exceptions change the result: keep (the licence's own status), denied, or allowed and review, which apply only to the licences in the exception's bases (GPL-2.0 and GPL-3.0, -only, -or-later or +). The allowed and review GPL exceptions were a builder addition, adopted as rules by decision D81 (settled). On any other licence an allowed or review exception changes nothing except that the result is at least review, so a denied licence stays denied (AGPL-3.0-only WITH GCC-exception-3.1 is denied). Any other exception makes the result at least review. The team's own licence (team_license) takes no exception at all.
rules.classifiers: Several License classifiers are read as alternatives; when they have different statuses and none of them is denied in that reading, the result is review, because classifiers do not say whether they are alternatives or parts.

organizer_base.description: Common CUDA base: torch 2.11.0+cu128 and its closure from the PyTorch cu128 index, installed read-only by the organizer from the official index on organizer machines. The organizer never redistributes these wheels; teams install them from the official index for development and do not ship them.
organizer_base.proprietary_patterns_note: PyTorch, triton and the NVIDIA CUDA library wheels: the CUDA 12 ones carry a -cu12 suffix, the CUDA 13 ones have none (nvidia-cublas, nvidia-cuda-runtime, ...). Any other nvidia-* package that declares LicenseRef-NVIDIA-Proprietary is treated the same way. Other nvidia-* packages, such as the BSD-3-Clause NVML binding nvidia-ml-py, are checked by their own licence.
organizer_base.scope: In a Stage 1 bundle every name in packages and every proprietary pattern is denied. In a Stage 2 web system only the proprietary patterns are denied (the web system's own environment may use open-source packages such as jinja2).
organizer_base.embedded_reason: The package contains NVIDIA binaries (file names in its wheel or RECORD) under NVIDIA's terms; the organizer decides whether it may be shipped.

packages_note: Name rules. names: exact package names, glob patterns (@mui/x-*-pro) or npm scope prefixes ending in / (@ckeditor/). min_version: the rule applies from that version on (an unknown version counts as matching). status denied or review flags the package whatever its metadata says; note adds the reason to the item's conditions; allowed records a published policy ruling that applies to every team (state the decision and date in reason) and clears a review or denied licence result, unless a denied or review rule for the same package also matches; it clears the review of NVIDIA binaries inside the package only with "embedded_binaries_ok": true. Rulings are made only by changing this file; there are no per-team exceptions (D63).

models.rule: Decision D64 (2026-10-10), replacing the D53 allowlist: the public models a team may use are exactly those of the model catalogue (catalog), named in submission.json by catalog_id; the organizer provides them offline in the read-only model store (APCTT_MODEL_STORE), and a model given by repo is that catalogue model only at the catalogue's revision. Any other public model is refused (denied), whatever its licence, because it is not available offline and public weights are not shipped; a catalogue model shipped in the bundle (path) is refused too. The deny list below still names well-known refusals. An entry with "team_trained": true and a path is the team's own weights, covered by the team licence: fine-tunes and adapters of a catalogue model name it in base_model (a catalogue id); a base_model, repo or url that is not a catalogue model is refused; the deny list applies to its names; a declared licence other than MIT is denied (the team licence, D72); the weights stay subject to the licence of the catalogue model they derive from (keep its LICENSE and NOTICE); and a name that suggests a model family (name_families, e.g. my-gemma-ft) other than its declared catalogue base_model is review. Weight files and shared libraries in assets/ and participant_module/ that no entry covers are review. No exceptions (D63).

datasets.note: Teams declare the licence or terms of every data source (declaration.json data_sources[].license), read like any other declared licence string: allowed licences pass; non-commercial, research-only and other denied terms are denied (D63: no exceptions); share-alike (CC-BY-SA), weak copyleft and unrecognised terms are review. A rule since decision D81 (settled).

web.note: --web reads npm packages from package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json (v2/v3 packages), else node_modules/.package-lock.json, else node_modules/*/package.json, else the names in package.json (licence not read: review); devDependencies and "dev": true entries are listed in a note, not as items, and those that are not allowed make one review item per project (a build may bundle them); "devOptional": true entries (a dev dependency that is also an optional dependency of a shipped package) are counted. Workspace packages (lock entries outside node_modules/, and their link entries) are the team's own code and are read once. A folder below the web root with its own package.json that no npm lock or node_modules/ installs is a vendored third-party item when it names a package the packages rules list (pdfjs-dist, apexcharts, handsontable: wherever it sits), when it is under a vendor-like folder (vendor_dir_names), or when it is inside a project with a lock and declares no dependencies or devDependencies (only optionalDependencies or peerDependencies, as pdfjs-dist does): its own licence and name rules are read and its runtime dependencies (dependencies, optionalDependencies, peerDependencies) not yet listed are review items with the name rules applied. It is the team's own sub-project instead (team licence, package.json names, yarn/pnpm/bun lock not read) when it has "private": true, "workspaces" or its own yarn, pnpm or bun lock, or otherwise when it declares dependencies or devDependencies; a refused sub-project licence then says to put a copied package under vendor/. The name rules apply to the package.json of every project folder too. Python packages: requirements*.txt and requirements*.lock (exact == pins), every *.whl and every installed package (*.dist-info, *.egg-info, PKG-INFO), virtual environments included. unread_dependency_files are review unless a requirements file sits next to them (yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml and bun.lock only when there is no npm lock and no node_modules/). Plain .js/.mjs/.cjs/.css files are never read: a folder with minified files (*.min.*), and outside an npm project a vendor-like or build output folder (build_output_dirs), is one review item; the team's own sources and the build output of an npm project are not listed. Fonts, images and other files are not checked.
